sections.title: Stage 4 · Adept: all 34 formulas
sections.html:
Stage 4 · Adept: all 34 formulas

Eight lessons that finish the bead rules. Eight combination moves use both friends at once, and after them nothing new ever happens on a rod.

Where this stage goes

The level goal. Master the eight combination formulas, so every possible move is automatic, and solve 3-digit problems.

In plain words. Every bead move is automatic. Three-digit sums, ten rows long. The first real sums in the head. No new rules after this. Everything from here is speed and the picture.

How long. 5–6 weeks at fifteen minutes a day, six days a week.

Try 6 + 6 on one rod. The big friend says: take away 4, carry 1. But the rod shows 6 as the top bead and one bottom bead. There is no 4 to take away.

So take the 4 away with a small friend: top bead up, one bead back. Then carry. That is a combination move. Both friends in one go.

There are eight of them, four adds and four take-aways, and they only show up in a few spots. Once they are learned, your child knows all 34 moves. Everything after this stage is speed, size and the picture in the head.

The drills in this stage

  • Two rods. The combination moves, found for you. A combo only happens when the rod shows 5 to 8 for an add, or 1 to 4 for a take-away.
  • Written. Six-line columns with every move, then 3-digit columns, then ten rows.
  • Timed. The ten-row page has a clock and a fridge chart.
  • Dictation. Read a 3-digit column out loud and let your child work it with nothing written.
  • Mental. Five one-digit numbers with any move, then two and three 2-digit numbers in the head.

Accuracy before speed

The pass marks stay at 9 of 10 on the two-rod pages and 85 percent on the columns. The ten-row page is the only one with a time target, and it still needs 8 of 10 right. A new move always costs speed for a week. That is the price of the move, and it is worth it.

Where this sits on the abacus ladders

Adept closes the Foundation level in UCMAS terms. Three-digit columns on the abacus go past the 10th kyu abacus format. In the head, two 2-digit numbers is Bead Score rung 5, and three 2-digit numbers with plus and minus is rung 6. Rung 6 is about where the trainer's chart puts a typical adult.

The 8 moves of this stage

In this book these moves are purple. Adds first, then take-aways.

MoveOn the beadsSay it
Plus 6+6 = −5 +1 +10take away 5, add 1, carry 1
Plus 7+7 = −5 +2 +10take away 5, add 2, carry 1
Plus 8+8 = −5 +3 +10take away 5, add 3, carry 1
Plus 9+9 = −5 +4 +10take away 5, add 4, carry 1
Minus 6−6 = +5 −1 −10add 5, take away 1, borrow 1
Minus 7−7 = +5 −2 −10add 5, take away 2, borrow 1
Minus 8−8 = +5 −3 −10add 5, take away 3, borrow 1
Minus 9−9 = +5 −4 −10add 5, take away 4, borrow 1
Parent linePraise the formula said out loud more than the right answer.

sections.title: Lesson 4.1 · Combo adds: 6+6, 7+7, 8+8, 5+9
sections.html:
Lesson 4.1 · Combo adds: 6+6, 7+7, 8+8, 5+9

Lesson 26 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 1 of 8. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can add 6, 7, 8 or 9 to a rod showing 5 to 8, using both friends and a carry.

The move

Watch the order. Top bead up. Friend beads up. Then carry. Three moves, one formula.

Plus 6 is "take away 5, add 1, carry 1". Plus 7 is "take away 5, add 2, carry 1". Plus 8 adds 3, and plus 9 adds 4, both with the same top bead up and the same carry.

Why it works: plus 6 is take away 4 and carry. Taking away 4 from a rod that shows the top bead needs a small friend. Take away 5, give back 1.

Worked example. Start at 5. Add 9, then 7.

  • Start with .
  • + 9. Ones rod, plus 9: take away 5, add 4, carry 1. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • + 7. Ones rod, plus 7: take away 3, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 21.
Parent lineHave your child say all three parts of the move out loud, slowly, for the first week.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then add the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345
15 + 985 + 837 + 747 + 676 + 6
678910
18 + 675 + 967 + 685 + 988 + 6

Stuck? Small friends make 5: 1 and 4, 2 and 3. Cannot add 3? Add 5 and take away 2. Big friends make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. Cannot add 8? Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left. Both friends at once: cannot add 7 and the heaven bead is already down? Take away 5, add 2, carry 1.

Lesson 4.2 · Combo take-aways: 11−6, 12−7, 13−8, 14−9

Lesson 27 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 2 of 8. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can take away 6, 7, 8 or 9 from a rod showing 1 to 4, using both friends and a borrow.

The move

11 − 6: add 4, the big friend of 6, to the ones rod. But the ones rod shows 1, and 1 + 4 needs a small friend: top bead down, take 1 away. Then borrow 1 from the tens.

So minus 6 is "add 5, take away 1, borrow 1". Minus 7 takes away 2. Minus 8 takes away 3. Minus 9 takes away 4.

Watch the order. Top bead down. Friend beads go. Then borrow.

Worked example. Start at 11. Take away 6.

  • Start with .
  • − 6. Ones rod, minus 6: add 5, take away 1, borrow 1. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 5.
Parent lineIf a combo stalls, ask "what does the big friend need?" and let your child find the small friend inside it.

Drill

Set the first number on two rods. Then take away the digit. Watch the tens rod. Write what the beads show. Pass mark: 9 of 10 right. Not yet? Same page tomorrow.

12345

678910
62 − 672 − 743 − 664 − 964 − 8

Take away 2 and carry 1 to the left. Both friends at once: cannot add 7 and the heaven bead is already down? Take away 5, add 2, carry 1.

Lesson 4.3 · All 34 formulas, mixed

Lesson 28 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 3 of 8. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can work 6-line columns that use every one of the 34 moves.

The move

Every rule, in one drill. On each rod, in order: are the beads free? Is it a small friend? Does it fit? If not, big friend. And if the big friend is not there, combo.

From here on, nothing new ever happens on a rod. Fluency is the whole game now.

Every sum on this page has at least one combo move in it. Slow is fine. Correct is the target.

Worked example. Start at 34. Add 28, then take away 17.

Lesson 4.4 · Three digits

Lesson 29 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 4 of 8. About 15 minutes. You need your abacus and a grown-up beside you.

By the end, your child can work 5-line columns of 3-digit numbers, with carries across all three rods.

The move

Three rods instead of two. Nothing else changes. Hundreds, then tens, then ones.

A carry can now run from the ones rod all the way to the hundreds. Each one is a plus 1 on the next rod, with the same rules as always.

Keep the eyes one rod ahead of the hand.

Lesson 4.6 · Mental: five single digits, all formulas

Lesson 31 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 6 of 8. About 8 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add and take away five one-digit numbers in the head, with any of the 34 moves.

The move

Abacus away. Five one-digit numbers, plus and minus. Every move is allowed now.

Picture the rod and the carry rod beside it. When the total crosses ten, a bead lands on the left. When it drops below, a bead comes back.

Worked example. Picture two empty rods. Five numbers.

  • Start with .
  • + 6. Ones rod, plus 6: the beads are free. Now .
  • + 8. Ones rod, plus 8: take away 5, add 3, carry 1. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • − 9. Ones rod, minus 9: add 5, take away 4, borrow 1. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • + 7. Ones rod, plus 7: take away 5, add 2, carry 1. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • − 5. Ones rod, minus 5: add 5, borrow 1 from the left. Tens rod, the borrow (minus 1): the beads are there. Now .
  • Read it: 7.
Parent lineRead the column out loud once if your child asks, then stay quiet until the answer.

Lesson 4.7 · Mental: two 2-digit numbers

Lesson 32 of 76. Stage 4, lesson 7 of 8. About 10 minutes. You need no abacus. A pencil for the answers only.

By the end, your child can add two 2-digit numbers in the head.

The move

Now two rods in the picture. 34 + 28: tens first, 3 and 2 make 5. Then ones: 4 and 8 will not fit, so take away 2 and carry. Say 62.

If it falls apart, set 34 + 28 on the real abacus. Watch it. Close your eyes and replay it. Then try the next one in the head.

Research on mental abacus users finds the picture holds about three or four rods at once. Two digits feels like a jump because your child is now holding two objects, each with its own beads.

Worked example. Picture 34. Add 28.

  • Start with .
  • + 28. Tens rod, plus 2: add 5, take away 3. Ones rod, plus 8: take away 2, carry 1 to the left. Tens rod, the carry (plus 1): the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 62.
Parent lineExpect this page to take a few days, because two rods in the head is a real jump.

The move

Three lines, two digits, adding only.

Keep the running total as a picture, never as words. If your child catches themselves saying "sixty-two" in their head, it is time to go back to the beads for one sum.

  • + 17. Tens rod, plus 1: the beads are free. Ones rod, plus 7: the beads are free. Now .
  • Read it: 79.

sections.title: The Adept Boss
sections.html:
The Adept Boss

Take the boss when all eight lessons are passed. Part 1 maps to Lessons 4.1 and 4.2. Part 2 maps to 4.4. Part 3 maps to 4.8. A child who passes this boss knows every bead move there is.

The printed test is Boss 4 in boss-tests.md. It has 3 parts:

  • Combo moves. 10 moves on your abacus. Need 9 of 10 in 2 minutes 30 seconds.
  • 3-digit, 5 lines. 6 problems on your abacus. Need 5 of 6 in 6 minutes.
  • Mental. 5 problems, three 2-digit numbers each. Need 4 of 5 in 3 minutes.

sections.title: What the trainer adds to this stage
sections.html:
What the trainer adds to this stage

The combination moves are the hardest to explain in words and the easiest to see. The trainer shows each one in slow motion: top bead up, friend back, carry. Two views of that and most children have it.

The trainer also hunts for combo spots. They are rare in random sums, so a paper sheet can go a whole page without one. The two-rod drill on screen serves them up every time.

And it keeps the best ten-row result, so a new best is on the screen the moment it lands.
